title: Phase-Coherent Spin and Lattice Modulations in a Y-type Hexaferrite
authors: Oskar Stepančić, Annika Stellhorn, Emma Campillo, Kun Zhai, Niklas Ekström, A. Corani, D. Alba Venero, R. Cubitt, E. Blackburn, L. Shen
abstract: Spin-driven multiferroics owe their electric polarization to lattice distortions that follow the magnetic order, yet in incommensurate magnets symmetry normally forbids such a distortion at the fundamental magnetic wavevector, and the distortions themselves are rarely observed. Here we use half-polarized neutron scattering to show that the Y-type hexaferrite Ba$_{0.4}$Sr$_{1.6}$Mg$_2$Fe$_{12}$O$_{22}$ hosts, in its saturated high-field state, a magnetic modulation and a longitudinal lattice modulation at one and the same wavevector, locked in phase. The signature is a large nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry, $r$ ~ 0.8, of the same sign at the two conjugate satellites and persisting to 275 K. The zone contrast and the field dependence of the satellite indicate an internal, field-induced longitudinal distortion. The modulated state coexists with the transverse-conical magnetoelectric phase and outlives it, revealing a fundamental-wavevector spin-lattice coupling in a magnetic field regime previously regarded as a simple ferrimagnet.
summary: This experiment uses polarized neutron scattering on a hexaferrite multiferroic to probe spin-lattice coupling. By measuring the nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry at satellite peaks, the authors reveal a robust, field-induced longitudinal lattice distortion locked in phase with the magnetic modulation. This confirms fundamental magnetoelastic coupling in a high-field regime previously misunderstood.
main_problem: The study investigates the elusive spin-lattice coupling in spin-driven multiferroics, specifically observing a magnetic modulation and a longitudinal lattice modulation locked in phase at the same wavevector.
main_result: The Y-type hexaferrite $	ext{Ba}_{0.4}	ext{Sr}_{1.6}	ext{Mg}_2	ext{Fe}_{12}	ext{O}_{22}$ exhibits a robust, field-induced, phase-coherent spin-lattice coupling signature ($r \simeq 0.8$) at the $	ext{k}_3$ satellite, persisting to high temperatures.
method: The research employs half-polarized neutron scattering to measure the nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry ($r$) at magnetic satellite peaks.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Y-type hexaferrite $	ext{Ba}_{0.4}	ext{Sr}_{1.6}	ext{Mg}_2	ext{Fe}_{12}	ext{O}_{22}$, a multiferroic material. The analysis focuses on the magnetic and lattice structure factors associated with incommensurate modulations.
key_observables: Nuclear-magnetic interference asymmetry ($r$), intensity evolution of $	ext{k}_2$ and $	ext{k}_3$ satellites, and field/temperature dependence of these signals.
important_parameters: High magnetic field regime (up to $7 	ext{ T}$), temperature range up to $275 	ext{ K}$, and the specific wavevectors $	ext{k}_2$ and $	ext{k}_3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the observed asymmetry originates from nuclear-magnetic interference, and that the modulation involves relative atomic displacements rather than a rigid translation of the basis.
figures_summary: Figures show the field evolution of scattering intensities revealing the $	ext{k}_3$ satellite, and compare the temperature dependence of the asymmetries ($r$) for $	ext{k}_2$ (null) versus $	ext{k}_3$ (large and persistent).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the necessity of probing spin-lattice coupling, using neutron scattering to detect the $	ext{k}_3$ satellite, quantifying the coupling via the asymmetry $r$, and finally interpreting this as a field-induced, phase-coherent magnetoelastic order.
why_interesting: This work provides direct experimental evidence of fundamental-wavevector spin-lattice coupling in a magnetic field regime, which is crucial for understanding magnetoelectric effects in complex oxides, linking magnetic order directly to structural distortion.
